merged_body: Rust-engine memoization caches must key on EVERYTHING the cached value depends on, not just the input expression. interpreter/concretize_cache.rs::bv_cache_key has now been the site of three separate wrong-answer bugs of exactly this shape: angr-owr37 (nested leaf identity dropped -> two distinct addresses collided), angr-9ke6b.89 (leaf variant untagged -> Concrete{value:N} vs Symbolic{id:N} collided), angr-360gt (producer CONFIG untagged -> a Multiple computed under read_range_limit=1024 was served to a store bound by write_range_limit=128, bypassing its Max fallback). The third is the subtle class: the key covered the input perfectly, but the cached value also depended on WHICH strategy chain produced it. Fix pattern: a namespace discriminant hashed into the key (see enum ConcretizeNs), not a post-hoc re-validation on hit — re-validation only works for shapes that carry their limit (TooLarge does; Multiple/Strided produced by the <=16 fast-enum path do not, since that path never consults the limit). When adding a new consumer to a shared cache, ask what config the entry was computed under; if it can differ, give it its own namespace. SECOND RULE (was invariant-bv-cache-key-variant-tag): a call-site precondition NEVER justifies dropping a field from a RECURSIVE hash/key function. bv_cache_key's 'all call sites early-return on as_u64(), so Concrete/Constrained never reach here' argument scopes only to the TOP-LEVEL value; hash_bv recurses into Expression operands where those variants are routine — angr-fs8kb.65 dropped Constrained's value field under exactly that justification, making Add(y,Constrained{id:5,value:10}) and Add(y,Constrained{id:5,value:20}) hash identically (a guaranteed collision). Every arm hashes its full payload, and do not reintroduce a 'cheap' untagged leaf shortcut for perf (the symbolic-leaf hash is ns against a Z3 concretize call; bench gate showed no movement). Details live on bv_cache_key / hash_bv in interpreter/concretize_cache.rs.

merged_body:
INVARIANT (ccall guest-width truncation): a sub-64-bit guest's ccall flag helper computes in u64, so it MUST mask both its dep inputs and the arithmetic result to the guest width before extracting a flag bit. The dispatch site's RustBV::concrete(result, ret_bits) does NOT rescue an unmasked helper — it truncates 0x1FFFFFFFF to 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. turns garbage into different garbage instead of erroring. angr-03vl4.72: vex/ccall/arm32.rs::armg_calc_flag_n was the lone ARM32 per-flag helper without it, so ARMG_CC_OP_SUB with dep1=0,dep2=1 returned 0xFFFFFFFF for the N flag instead of 1, live on the standalone armg_calculate_flag_n CCall arm (taken whenever all four args are concrete). Its siblings armg_calc_flag_z/_c/_v mask on entry and mask each wrapping_* result; arm64 gets it for free via the shared arm64_res helper. When adding or reviewing a per-flag helper for a 32-bit guest, check BOTH masks — entry-only masking still lets a borrowing subtract sign-extend into the high half. Sibling rule: [invariant-ccall-flag-mask-named-constants].

X86/AMD64 HALF (was invariant-calc-flags-sub-unmasked): all six raw-operand concrete flag builders in vex/ccall/x86_concrete.rs — calc_flags_add/sub/adc/sbb/umul/smul — mask their operands to get_mask(nbits) BEFORE use, matching the symbolic siblings in x86_symbolic.rs which extract_to_nbits unconditionally (add/sub angr-36vvn.3; umul/smul angr-0jh0j.69: umul's hi = (prod >> nbits) & mask picked up cross-term garbage from bits above the width, wrecking CF/OF, and sign_extend_to_i64's non-negative branch returned val verbatim so nbits=8 val=0x100 multiplied as 256 instead of 0). Gate: ccall_tests.rs::diff_fuzz_sym_flags_unmasked_inputs diffs concrete vs symbolic over Add/Sub/Adc/Sbb/Logic/Umul/Smul with UNMASKED random operands and pins that masking inputs changes nothing. When adding a new concrete flag builder that takes raw operands, mask first and extend that test's category list — every other diff_fuzz_sym_flags_* pre-masks and cannot see this bug class.

merged_body: RustBV::Concrete stores its value in a u128 (16 bytes / 128 bits max) regardless of declared width. Four hazard families follow. (1) ASSEMBLY: any code that ASSEMBLES a concrete value wider than 16 bytes by funneling bytes through a u128 is BUGGY: the shift wraps mod 128 in release (panics in debug), OR-ing high bytes back over low bytes. Fixed sites (commit df4bb4cd3, bd angr-tk7yv): memory/load.rs::load_concrete (two copies -- eager + lazy paths) now assemble size>16 loads as a Concat of per-byte concretes; symbolic/value_ops.rs::concat_into AND concat_no_ctx now guard the concrete-fold with 'if result_width <= 128' (else keep a Concat expression); exploration/state_api.rs::_get_state_memory reads in <=16-byte chunks. Also interpreter/bv_utils.rs::bytes_to_bv (angr-03vl4.31, commits 7608c8814 + 00b619214) -- the VEX-side twin of memory/load.rs::bytes_to_bv, reached from expressions.rs load fast paths, mod.rs read_memory and statements_dirty.rs::handle_dirty_call; it folds >16-byte inputs into a Concat via concat_no_ctx (high byte first: a.concat(b) puts a above b). Also interpreter/expressions.rs::eval_const's IRConst::V256 arm (angr-03vl4.29, commit 6ac725232) -- it packed v[0]|v[1]<<64 into ONE concrete tagged width 128, dropping v[2]/v[3]; now high.concat_no_ctx(&low) of the two 128-bit halves. Note the acceptance criteria said 'just retag the width as 256', which alone would have kept the truncation -- a wide width tag on a Concrete is a LIE, not a fix. Symptom seen: get_state_memory(24) on xmllint rodata returned chunk0|chunk2. Affects 32-byte AVX (ymm) concrete loads too. INVARIANT for future code: never pack >16 concrete bytes into a u128; build wide concretes via per-byte/per-chunk Concat, and do NOT 'fix' the overflow by clamping at 16 bytes -- that trades an abort for a silently truncated value. (2) BIT-SLICING (was invariant-concrete-extract-width128): bits at position >= 128 of a wider-than-128 Concrete (e.g. a 192-bit Multi-cell value) are logically zero, and RustBV::as_u128() returns Some for ANY Concrete width. Any bit-slicing on a concrete fast path (e.g. extract_into in symbolic/value_ops.rs) MUST guard BOTH: shift-by-low (v >> low overflows when low >= 128 -> result is 0) AND mask (1u128 << result_width overflows at result_width >= 128 -> use u128::MAX). Fixed in angr-dondi; mirrors the same width>=128 mask guard already in RustBV::concrete() (value.rs). (3) VEC-OP WIDENING (angr-sqfj8.118): adding 256-bit lane shapes to a vex/opcode_map*.rs parse arm (vector shapes live in opcode_map_vector.rs) silently makes that op's evaluator concrete fast path reachable at total_width=256, where 'result |= lane << lo' shifts a u128 by up to 192. Before widening ANY vector op family to V256, check its evaluator carries the 'if total_width <= 128' guard that vec_int_lane_op (ops/vec_int_lane.rs) has -- vec_shift_n (ops/vec_shift.rs; the merged shift-by-immediate helper that replaced vec_shl_n/vec_shr_n/vec_sar_n in angr-5mnx3.68) did not until .118. Applied again in angr-sqfj8.112 (V256 CmpEQ/CmpGT): vec_int_lane_op's existing guard is why that widening needed no evaluator change. The float lane ops were the last V256 op-coverage gap and are now covered too (angr-fs8kb.15, ops/tests_vec_float_lane.rs::test_vec_float_binops_avx2_256_bit_f32x8 and ::test_vec_float_min_max_sqrt_avx2_256_bit_f64x4); vec_float_lane_op's 'if total_width <= 128' guard was already present and correct. (4) SERIALIZATION (angr-03vl4.4): the reverse direction, RustBV -> bytes, has the mirror overflow ('value >> (i*8)' for i up to 31). interpreter/bv_utils.rs::bv_to_bytes stops at 16 bytes and zero-fills above, which IS correct there because as_u128() only ever exposes the low 128 bits -- but it means bv_to_bytes CANNOT serialize a wide Concat (as_u128() is None -> it returns all zeros); the reject_symbolic_byte_store guard is what keeps that from silently zeroing memory. callbacks/dispatch.rs used to carry a byte-identical private copy of bv_to_bytes that inherited every bug; it now imports interpreter::bv_utils::bv_to_bytes (which is pub(crate) for exactly that reason). Test pattern for a >128-bit op: build operands with concat_into of two 128-bit concretes and assert one extracted lane at a time (ops/tests_vec_int_lane.rs::test_vec_cmp_avx2_256_bit_i32x8); for the byte conversions see interpreter/bv_utils_tests.rs::bytes_to_bv_of_256_bit_buffer_keeps_every_byte_via_concat. ADDENDUM (was invariant-concrete-bv-width128-shift-guard): hazard (2)'s guards apply to EVERY concrete op that shifts/masks by a bit POSITION, not only extract_into — extract_no_ctx had the same window logic without the guards until angr-ph300.31 and aborted/mis-extracted on 256-bit ymm sub-register overlays (arch/register_file.rs callers). Any new concrete BV op that shifts by a bit position must copy extract_into's guards (shift=0 when low>=128, mask=u128::MAX when result_width>=128); operand-amount narrowing is the separate rule in invariant-concrete-shift-clamp-before-narrow.

merged_body: A code example that appears in BOTH a docs/*.rst worked example and a Rust module doc (//!) is one logical example with N copies, and a signature change reaches only the copy the author happened to be looking at. Concrete recurrence: angr-c7xno.64 fixed the stale 3-arg scan_for_null(state, addr, MAX_STRLEN) in simprocedures.rst -- and missed a SECOND copy 150 lines lower in the same file plus a third in procedures/macros.rs's module doc; both survived until angr-0jh0j.41/.39 two rounds later. RULE: when a shared helper's signature or dispatch changes, grep the helper/symbol name across docs/**/*.rst AND native/angr/src/**/*.rs doc comments -- not just the one file you are editing, and not just once per file (grep -n, count the hits, fix all of them). The line-citation gate (tools/check_line_citations.py) does NOT catch this class: a wrong argument list carries no line number. Same reasoning as refactor-memory-sweep-rule, applied to doc copies instead of bd memories. GUARD-DRIFT COROLLARY (was invariant-doc-worked-example-guard-drift): a fix that adds a *guard* to a function used as a worked example in docs/ must update that example in the same commit. Round-5 instances: simprocedures.rst 'Worked example 3: malloc' lost NativeMalloc's check_max(size, MAX_ALLOC_SIZE)? when angr-03vl4.53 added it (the section had been refreshed one commit earlier for an unrelated reason, so 'recently touched' is no evidence of currency), and rust_vex_ops.rst's BYPASS matrix kept a dead Iop_Perm8x32 after angr-sqfj8.117 remapped the family. Worse than ordinary doc rot because examples are COPIED — a missing guard propagates the hole into every new procedure written from it. No CI gate sees this class; applies to any declare_proc!/register_procs! sample, VEX opcode table or API snippet.
